<reason>A established a narrow emergency exception and defended it against B’s strongest objection: advance validation, automatic expiry, and targeted hardship assistance need not require capacity to review every case before disbursement. B compellingly explained wrongful-deprivation risks, but repeatedly treated guaranteed later review as though no suspension had occurred beforehand. Its sweeping claims that historical scandals contained the same safeguards also failed to establish equivalence. A more convincingly resolved the timing, enforceability, and proportionality clashes.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>A’s strongest response was that insufficient review triggers automatic restoration, not indefinite withholding. Combined with the distinction between immediate universal review and subsequent targeted review, this substantially weakened B’s claim that reviewer scarcity necessarily makes the exception unsafe.</best_rebuttal>
